title: MetaLeak: Uncovering Side Channels in Secure Processor Architectures Exploiting Metadata
problem: Metadata management schemes in secure processor architectures (integrity trees and counters) create timing variations that can be exploited to leak information. Security mechanisms intended to protect confidentiality and integrity inadvertently introduce new microarchitectural side channel vectors.
motivation: Existing microarchitecture security research examines performance optimizations and security mechanisms separately, leaving unexplored the holistic impact of integrated security mechanisms on information leakage in secure processors.
method: MetaLeak measures tiny timing differences in how secure processors access and update metadata—the bookkeeping information used to verify data hasn't been tampered with (integrity trees) and to prevent data replay attacks (counters). MetaLeak-T exploits timing patterns when multiple processor cores access the shared integrity tree, while MetaLeak-C does the same by watching counter state changes. These timing measurements leak secrets because an attacker on one core can observe how long security operations take on another core without explicitly sharing data with the victim.
key_novelty: Integrity trees and counters—metadata that secure processors use to protect data—can be systematically exploited as timing side channels to leak secrets to attackers.
contributions: First comprehensive side channel exploration of secure processor architectures with hardware-based confidentiality and integrity protection
Two attack variants exploiting integrity tree and counter metadata with 97% accuracy secret exfiltration
End-to-end attack framework demonstrating cross-core and cross-socket covert communication via security metadata
Identification that fundamental metadata mechanisms are the root cause, necessitating leakage-taming techniques in future secure processor designs
primary_theme: metadata-based side channels in secure processors
